text: Plan: write docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md as a requirements-traceable architecture, with the power path, USB-C attachment, common active protection, parallel outputs, LED, mechanical implementation, and explicit MCU/firmware non-applicability. Preserve the 4.75–5.25 V range, full 500 mA external load, strictly below 2 mA unloaded input, quantity-100 BOM below USD 8, and 40 × 30 mm envelope. The MIC2544 programming-current boundary, guaranteed current-limit range, leakage, visibility, and exact component suitability remain acceptance risks, not verified compliance. Read related capability specs and check candidate library identity before documenting pin-level proposals; no KiCad edits are planned.

args.why: Stage 2 needs a reviewable subsystem architecture for the independent protected USB-C 500 mA breakout. The specification already fixes the product budgets, but candidate-part evidence and the unloaded-current sum are not closed. Document the intended topology, all assumptions, and explicit selection gates without promoting supplied research into verified device guarantees or manufacturing results.
args.what_changes:
- Create or surgically update docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md with a prose block diagram and one section per subsystem: USB-C input and attachment, active protection and power distribution, parallel external outputs, protected-rail LED/UI, MCU/firmware and data-connectivity applicability, mechanical/manufacturing, and verification interfaces.
- Carry forward exact requirements, net-name conventions, proposed pin assignments, current-accounting bins, and normal/startup/fault distinctions. Explain every decision and intentional omission.
- Keep MIC2544-2YM, 301 ohm RSET, LED/decoupling choices, connector mappings, and price observations conditional wherever evidence remains incomplete. Separate installed-library observations from manufacturer suitability evidence.
- Define hard acceptance gates for the strictly below 2 mA unloaded input current, full 500 mA external load plus board demand, source/cable capability, fault heating/recovery, cost, and mechanical fit. Do not relax budgets or add programmable hardware.
- Record non-trivial architecture decisions and any new architecture constraints through the provided tools; update affected design/specification documentation only if an actual stated assumption or decision changes. No schematic, board, fabricated test result, or firmware artifact is created in this stage.
args.tasks:
- [ ] Read any existing subsystem document and the related OpenSpec capability specs; preserve applicable established content.
- [ ] Check the candidate active-device symbol, actual library pins, and candidate footprints; label exactly what these checks do and do not prove.
- [ ] Write docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md with the complete prose topology and subsystem reasoning/key values, including distinct CC1/CC2 Rd, both outputs and LED after common active protection, load-only outputs, and MCU/firmware non-applicability.
- [ ] Reconcile the complete non-overlapping unloaded-current framework and mark the 1.791 mA sum as an allocation only; require a justified worst-case total strictly below 2 mA before candidate acceptance. Explicitly reject any candidate that cannot meet it rather than assuming the 1 mA programming bin is satisfied.
- [ ] Document current-limit lower-bound acceptance above 500 mA plus protected-rail demand and upper-bound fault/thermal design obligations; preserve voltage, assembly, board size, stackup, and cost targets.
- [ ] Record decisions and newly stated constraints; synchronize any affected docs and explain intentional absent components.
- [ ] Run check_drift and reconcile its actual report. Apply ERC/DRC/legibility only where source edits make them applicable; do not claim checks or bench tests that did not run.
- [ ] Read back the architecture and finish through the original stage gate, resolving any reported obligations.
